children: Russia is not considering raising taxes, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, the same day authorities reported a narrowing budget deficit that nonetheless remained well above the government's annual target.

The finance ministry, citing preliminary data, said the  deficit narrowed to 5.8 trillion roubles ($67.8 billion), or 2.5% of gross domestic product, in the first eight months of the year, from 6.46 trillion roubles, or 2.8% of GDP, a month earlier.
Even so, the deficit was 48% higher than in the same period last year and 53% above the full-year target.
Asked about the shortfall remaining above government expectations, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the figure "should not cause any concern".
"Macroeconomic stability is fully ensured," he said.
"The government is constantly addressing issues of economic development" including during meetings with President Vladimir Putin, Peskov added.
